land.text: the Crown's Ireland outside the Pale, Dublin and the Protestant enclaves: after the 1641 rising the Confederates 'controlled two-thirds of Ireland, including Waterford and Wexford' by the end of 1642

predecessors.note: The legal predecessor is the Crown of Ireland (a Kingdom of Ireland dossier, eu-11-x); Cliopatria's Kingdom of England row carries Ireland to 1641 and the royalist remnant of Ireland in 1648-1652.

land.text: Ireland, 'annexed by the Commonwealth of England' after the Cromwellian conquest of 1649-1653

successors.note: Kilkenny (March 1650), Waterford (1650), Limerick (1651) and Galway (May 1652) are the ledger's losses; the last organised force surrendered at Cavan in April 1653.

capitals.name: Kilkenny
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Kilkenny'; the first General Assembly met there on 24 October 1642; 'Kilkenny fell after a short siege in 1650' (March 1650 on the Irish Confederate Wars page). The page names no later seat.

union.text: Wexford, held by the Confederates by the end of 1642

correction.text: the 1642 shape plus County Wexford: 'the Confederacy controlled two-thirds of Ireland, including Waterford and Wexford'

keyframe_review.note: 61,366 km2 on Cliopatria (58,167 km2 on the grid, 69% of the island's 84,000 km2) against 'controlled up to two-thirds of Ireland' (Confederate Ireland page) and 'By the end of 1642 the Confederacy controlled two-thirds of Ireland, including Waterford and Wexford' (Irish Confederate Wars page): the area agrees (ratio about 1.0). The shape holds all of Connacht, most of Munster (Cork 24 cells, Kerry 16), a part of Leinster and a western half of Ulster, but none of County Wexford, which the page names as held, so Wexford is added.

union.text: Limerick, captured by Garret Barry in 1642

correction.text: the 1645 shape plus Kilkenny, Waterford, Wexford and Limerick, which the pages show in Confederate hands until Cromwell (Kilkenny March 1650, Waterford 1650, Limerick 1651)

keyframe_review.note: 43,854 km2, 52% of the island: the shape drops Kilkenny (the Confederate capital, 7 cells in 1642 and none here), Waterford, Limerick, Wexford and nearly all of Tipperary, yet no page opened records any such loss before 1649: the pages have the Confederates making the Cessation with Ormonde (15 September 1643), the Ormond Peace (28 March 1646) and winning at Benburb (June 1646), and Inchiquin giving Parliament only Cork, Kinsale and Youghal (July 1644; Cork falls from 24 to 20 cells here). The corrected shape restores the capital county and the towns the pages name. Region choices are the researcher's reading (towns to counties); the cuts of 1647 (Dungan's Hill, Knocknanuss) are undated on the page and not drawn.

correction.text: the 1648 shape plus Kilkenny and Wexford

keyframe_review.note: 56,540 km2: Munster and Connacht return but Kilkenny is again nearly absent (1 cell against 7 in 1642) and Wexford missing; the pages record the Inchiquin Truce with the Royalists (May 1648) and a Confederate dissolution of 1648 (Wars page, which conflicts with the 1652 end of the Confederate Ireland infobox), and nothing territorial before Cromwell's landing in August 1649. Same correction as 1645: add Kilkenny and Wexford. The page's 'Territorial changes: Ireland annexed by the Commonwealth of England' is carried by the ledger losses of 1650-1652.

region.text: 'controlled up to two-thirds of Ireland': Connacht, most of Munster, the south-east and western Ulster

ledger.note: 1642: the Irish Catholic Confederation is formed at Kilkenny. The first Confederate General Assembly was held there on 24 October 1642 (the 10 May 1642 clerical synod and the Supreme Council elected about 14 November are the page's other dates; infobox 'Established: 1642'). By early 1642 rebel concentrations stood in Ulster, the Pale, the south-east and the south-west, and Garret Barry took Limerick in 1642.

1642: the Pale and Dublin are fought over. By early 1642 rebel forces held 'the Pale around Dublin (Viscount Gormanstown)'; 'Over 1642, English forces re-established control over Dublin'. The page does not date the first campaign.
1643: the Cessation of Arms with the Royalists (15 September). 'The Confederates and Royalists signed a truce, or Cessation of Arms, on 15 September 1643'; Inchiquin in Cork rejected it.

region.text: Ireland, the Cromwellian conquest 15 August 1649 - 27 September 1653

ledger.note: 1649: Cromwell lands at Dublin (15 August) and the Cromwellian conquest begins. The Confederates and Royalists under Ormonde had been beaten at Rathmines on 2 August; 'In August 1649, a large English Parliamentarian army, led by Oliver Cromwell, invaded Ireland.'

region.text: Waterford, surrendered after a prolonged siege in 1650

ledger.note: 1650: Waterford falls. 'Waterford and Duncannon eventually surrendered after prolonged sieges in 1650.'
1650: Kilkenny, the Confederate capital, falls in March. 'Kilkenny was captured in March 1650' (Irish Confederate Wars); 'Kilkenny fell after a short siege in 1650' (Confederate Ireland page).
1652: Galway, the last Confederate stronghold, falls in May. 'Galway was captured in May 1652.' Connacht is the western province the Parliamentarians entered across the Shannon in October 1650.

1652: the Confederate-Royalist alliance is beaten. 'By May 1652 it had defeated the Confederate-Royalist alliance'; the Irish guerrilla leaders surrendered 'under terms signed at Kilkenny that May' (Cromwellian conquest page).

region.text: the Confederate lands at the end: Connacht and the west, whose last strongholds had fallen by May 1652

ledger.note: 1652: the Confederation ends with the Cromwellian conquest. Infobox 'Cromwellian conquest: 1652'; the Cromwellian conquest page (not this one) says guerrilla fighting lasted about a year longer: the last organised force surrendered at Cloughoughter on 27 April 1653 and the Commonwealth declared the rebellion subdued on 27 September 1653. The Irish Confederate Wars page instead says the association dissolved in 1648.

wars.name: Irish Confederate Wars
belligerents: Royalists under the Marquess of Ormonde

zones.text: Ireland: the Pale and Dublin, Cork and the Munster coast, Ulster and Connacht

wars.outcome: English Parliamentarian victory: the Confederates held up to two-thirds of Ireland in 1642 and lost it to the Cromwellian conquest of 1649-1653; 'Ireland annexed by the Commonwealth of England'.
wars.note: Infobox 23 October 1641 - 27 April 1653. Cessation of 15 September 1643, First Ormond Peace 28 March 1646, Ormonde hands Dublin to Michael Jones on 19 June 1647, Inchiquin defects to Parliament in July 1644 and to the Royalists in 1648 (month not on the page), Kilkenny falls March 1650, Galway May 1652.

wars.name: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
belligerents: Royalists under the Marquess of Ormonde
wars.outcome: Commonwealth victory; Ireland merged into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland.

certainty.note: Held 'up to two-thirds of Ireland' with no treaty or survey line; the extent shifts with the sieges (Waterford 1650, Kilkenny March 1650, Limerick 1651, Galway May 1652).

notes:
Written by eu-11-j on 2026-10-25 from three pages (budget 1-2; Cromwellian conquest page added because the Commonwealth dossier opened it).

Cliopatria's three shapes are all verdict 'adjust'. The 1645-1647 and 1648-1652 shapes omit Kilkenny (the Confederate capital) and other places the pages place in Confederate hands until 1650-1652; the corrections add Kilkenny, Waterford, Wexford and Limerick back. The 1642 shape lacks County Wexford. The region choices turn towns into counties, which is the researcher's reading; a gap-filler could open 'Confederate Ireland' sub-articles (Confederate Catholic army, Kilkenny Assembly) for the true extent per year. The Cork enclave under Inchiquin (July 1644 to Parliament; May 1648 truce with the Royalists) is a contest the pages do not date by area; not recorded as ledger events.

Pages disagree: Confederate Ireland infobox ends the state in 1652 (used); Irish Confederate Wars says the Confederates dissolved their association in 1648 and gives May or October for the 1642 formation (October used: first General Assembly 24 October 1642). The Second Ormond Peace (January 1649) is not on either page and is not recorded.

Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-england (royalist/Parliamentary English government in Dublin; eu-11), a Kingdom of Ireland or Ormonde's royalist Ireland (eu-11-x), 'Scottish Covenanter army in Ulster' (not a state), Inchiquin's Munster (not a state). No new region names needed (The Pale exists in the gazetteer).
